question: What is the main purpose of a physical examination in nursing?

options.A: To replace the need for a detailed patient medical history
options.B: To diagnose medical conditions independently without a doctor
options.C: To gather objective data about the patient's health status
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital paperwork requirements

explanation: A physical examination provides concrete, measurable facts about the body to complement what the patient tells you in their history. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is obtaining a baseline physical assessment during admission important?

options.A: It gives you a standard to compare future health changes against
options.B: It allows the nurse to discharge the patient much faster
options.C: It guarantees the patient will not develop new complications
options.D: It prevents the patient from asking questions about their care

explanation: Initial baseline data lets the nurse spot subtle improvements or sudden declines during the hospital stay. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: What should the nurse do first before starting a physical examination?

options.A: Ask the family members to leave the hospital room
options.B: Prepare the environment and gather needed equipment
options.C: Perform a deep tissue palpation of the abdomen

explanation: Organizing your tools and space beforehand prevents interruptions and keeps the patient calm and comfortable. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is it helpful to ask a patient to empty their bladder before an exam?

options.A: It ensures the patient can stand up without assistance
options.B: It completely prevents any risk of a urinary tract infection
options.C: It lowers the patient's blood pressure significantly
options.D: It makes abdominal palpation more comfortable and accurate

explanation: A full bladder can cause discomfort and make it difficult for the nurse to feel deep abdominal organs properly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: When should a nurse perform hand hygiene during a physical examination?

options.A: Only after touching visible body fluids
options.B: Before and after every patient contact
options.C: Only when the patient requests it
options.D: At the beginning of the work shift only

explanation: Regular hand hygiene is the single most effective way to stop the spread of harmful germs between patients. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT required under standard precautions for a routine physical check?

options.A: Wearing clean gloves if contact with body fluids is expected
options.B: Cleaning stethoscope bells and diaphragms between patients
options.C: Performing proper hand hygiene before touching the patient
options.D: Wearing a full sterile surgical gown for a simple pulse check

explanation: Routine physical checks do not require sterile surgical gowns unless you are performing a sterile invasive procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which assessment technique involves tapping the body surface to produce sounds?
explanation: Percussion uses finger taps to create vibrations, helping the nurse judge whether underlying tissues are air-filled, fluid-filled, or solid. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why does the standard physical assessment order change when examining a patient's abdomen?

options.A: Palpating too early can alter natural bowel sounds
options.B: Percussion must happen before looking at the skin
options.C: Inspection is completely unnecessary for abdominal exams
options.D: Auscultation is always painful for the patient

explanation: Pressing or pushing on the abdomen stimulates peristalsis, which would give you false readings when you try to listen to bowel sounds afterward. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: What does a general survey primarily evaluate?

options.A: The patient's complete financial and employment history
options.B: The microscopic cellular structure of body tissues
options.C: The patient's overall appearance and obvious behavior
options.D: The exact electrical conduction system of the heart

explanation: The general survey is a quick visual overview of how sick, comfortable, or distressed a patient looks right away. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which set of findings represents standard vital signs taken during a routine check?

options.A: Vision score, hearing clarity, and skin moisture
options.B: Height, weight, shoe size, and blood glucose level
options.C: Muscle strength, reflex speed, and joint flexibility
options.D: Temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure

explanation: These four measurements track core body functions and are universally tracked as primary vital signs. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which tool is most essential for assessing the respiratory and cardiovascular systems?
explanation: A stethoscope allows the nurse to hear internal sounds like heartbeats, valve closures, and air moving through lung fields. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a nurse assessing when checking a patient's neurological status during an exam?

options.A: The presence of bowel sounds in four quadrants
options.B: Orientation, reflexes, and overall mental function
options.C: The strength and rhythm of the apical pulse
options.D: The rate of air exchange in the lower lung lobes

explanation: Neurological checks look at brain function, nerve responses, and sensory processing to ensure the nervous system is working properly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: How should a nurse document physical assessment findings in a patient's chart?

options.A: Writing shorthand codes that only the nurse understands
options.B: Using personal opinions and general assumptions
options.C: Waiting until the end of the work week to write notes
options.D: Using clear, objective, and specific descriptive terms

explanation: Objective charting ensures that any healthcare provider reading the chart gets an exact and accurate picture of the patient's condition. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)

question: What should a nurse do immediately after finding abnormal, life-threatening changes during an exam?

options.A: Delete the entry from the computer to avoid alarming others
options.B: Ask the patient to walk around the room to see if it improves
options.C: Report the findings to the physician or charge nurse right away
options.D: Wait until the shift change report to mention it to anyone

explanation: Critical changes require prompt communication and action to ensure the patient gets emergency medical intervention quickly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)
